reported: three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:218 — the Workflow-mode note now claims the opposite of what the script does. "It also detects a fabricated sha. If the implementer reports a well-formed sha it never created, the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`." `three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js` cannot do this and says so at lines 237-242: "a fabricated sha does not survive into the returned `headSha`, but it is not itself detected ... Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository, which this script cannot do — it has no shell." The only sha handling in the script is `sha(v)` (phase.js:80), a 40-hex *shape* test, plus the equality test against `base` (phase.js:247) and the substitution of `gateHead` (phase.js:306-316). The replaced sentence was the only place in the skill where that limitation was written down — plan Decision D2 chose option (b) precisely because "deleting it loses the only place that limit is written down," and D2 also required the note be "restated from the script, not from memory." This inverts a documented limitation into a safety guarantee a reader will rely on.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — reviewers are now told to receive "the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest." This contradicts two other shipped files. `three-loop-workflow/SKILL.md:62`: "Reviewers are fresh subagents receiving the diff and the plan — and **nothing else**: not your summary of the change, not your session, not the reasoning that produced it." `three-loop-workflow/scripts/phase.js:328-332` excludes this exact input by name and gives the reason: "not its list of low-confidence areas, not an instruction about where to look: the value of a second reviewer is that it never saw the reasoning that produced the change, and a shared attention directive correlates the two readings it is there to keep independent. The new sentence also keeps the following clause "the value comes from their independence," which it has just undermined, and silently drops the old exclusions "not your summary of the change, and not the whole skill." It lands in the plan's Non-goals: "No change to ... any rule stated elsewhere in the skill."

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — "Fix every reported blocking finding, then triage: while the diff is still moving, confirming each claim first costs a round you will spend anyway." This reverses the repo's central ordering rule and contradicts the section immediately above it. build.md:70 (unchanged, twelve lines earlier): "**Do not fix a finding you have not confirmed.**" build.md:76: "**The confirmed count is what closes the phase**, not the reported one. Skipping triage means a phantom finding consumes a fix round and can exhaust the round cap on code that was already correct." SKILL.md:70: "**Triage before you fix, and before you count.**" phase.js:369-372: "Triage before counting ... reported: scripts/accept-release.sh:194 — the fabricated-sha sweep's negation filter is line-scoped and therefore defeated by the exact edit it exists to catch. `hits=$(grep -rnE 'detects? a fabricated sha' three-loop-workflow/ | grep -v 'does not detect a fabricated sha' || true)` filters whole LINES. build.md is written one-paragraph-per-line, and the negated sentence lives on line 218 with the rest of its paragraph, so any sentence added to that paragraph shares a line with the negation and is filtered out wholesale. Demonstrated in a fresh clone: appending "As of this release the script now detects a fabricated sha." to build.md:218 produced `ACCEPT: all checks passed`, exit 0, with no FAIL of any kind. The commit body of 19bf961 states the sweep "fails on any un-negated claim that the fabrication is detected" and the check's own comment calls it "Two-sided, because this one has regressed twice" — neither is true. The prior regression (4105e9d) was an edit to that same paragraph, i.e. the sweep passes on a rerun of the defect it was written for. Fix is paragraph- or sentence-scoping (the python3 paragraph-splitter already in this file at :325-343 is the in-repo precedent), not a wider grep.

scripts/accept-release.sh:206 — the `[ -f "$p" ]` fallback lets the shipped skill name a script that is not in the shipped skill, which is the exact failure the check's own comment at :202-203 says it prevents ("A reader told to run `scripts/x.sh` looks in the skill's own scripts/ directory, finds nothing"). Demonstrated: adding "Verify with `scripts/negative-test.sh`" to three-loop-workflow/references/build.md printed `ok referenced script exists: scripts/negative-test.sh` and `ACCEPT: all checks passed`. negative-test.sh exists only at the host repo root; a user with the skill installed at ~/.claude/skills/three-loop-workflow/ has no such file. The justification at :204 ("Both roots are accepted because the skill names its own scripts and the host repo's") is false about the tree it was written against: `grep -rohE 'scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.(js|sh)' three-loop-workflow --include='*.md' | sort -u` returns exactly one path, `scripts/phase.js` (10 occurrences). The host-root fallback covers nothing that exists and only weakens the check.

scripts/accept-release.sh:204-206 — the new script-path check accepts the host-repo root, which defeats the property the check exists to hold, and the comment justifying that fallback states something false about the tree. `[ -f "three-loop-workflow/$p" ] || [ -f "$p" ]` means a skill document that names `scripts/negative-test.sh`, `scripts/sim-phase.js`, `scripts/accept-release.sh` or `scripts/sim-scenarios.js` passes the gate, because those files exist at the repo root — while a reader of the *installed* skill at `~/.claude/skills/three-loop-workflow/` finds nothing there. That is precisely the failure edcc26d7 added this check for (`scripts/verify-plan.sh` resolved nowhere, and the commit message's own argument is "a reader follows this one there and finds nothing"). The comment at :204 says "Both roots are accepted because the skill names its own scripts and the host repo's" — I resolved every path the check extracts and the shipped skill names exactly one script, `scripts/phase.js`, which resolves inside the skill. No `.md` under `three-loop-workflow/` names a host-repo script, so the stated reason for the fallback is not true today, and the fallback only widens the hole. CLAUDE.md's norm is explicit here ("Do not claim a script does something without testing that it does"; a weakened gate "reads as coverage that is not there"). Restricting the test to `three-loop-workflow/$p` makes the check assert what its own header claims, and nothing currently in the skill would fail.

scripts/accept-release.sh:203 — `CLAIM = re.compile(r"detects? a fabricated sha")` is case-sensitive and matches only that one surface form, while the section reports "nothing in the shipped skill claims a fabricated sha is detected" (:220). Three near-neighbour claims appended to `build.md` all produced `ACCEPT: all checks passed`, exit 0, no FAIL: (a) "As of this release the script detects a fabricated SHA." — SHA is the conventional capitalisation of the acronym; (b) "The script detects fabricated shas." — plural, no article; (c) "The fabrication is detected by the guard." — the passive form, which is the wording the check's own FAIL message uses. `negative-test-accept.sh` A1/A2 pin only the single wording the sweep was built around, so the harness cannot see any of these.

scripts/accept-release.sh:204 — `NEG = re.compile(r"\bnot\b|\bnever\b|\bcannot\b|n't\b")` rejects correct prose. Demonstrated, each appended to `build.md` and each producing `FAIL  the shipped skill claims the fabrication is detected`: "Nothing in phase.js detects a fabricated sha." (`\bnot\b` does not match inside "Nothing"), "No part of the script detects a fabricated sha.", "The script is unable to detect a fabricated sha." All three are true statements the skill should be free to make, and two of them are more natural phrasings of the sentence the check is protecting. This is the disqualifier the same author applied to Item 5 in b805a76 — "a gate that fails on right writing is the same defect as one that passes on wrong writing" — applied to one check and not the other.

Plan scope — three of the four non-build.md files in this diff are outside both the Non-goals and the recorded exception. The Non-goals say "`build.md` only. No change to `SKILL.md`, to `phase.js`, or to any other file." D3 breaks it "once, for the gate" and states the cost precisely: "`scripts/accept-release.sh` is in the diff, so this is no longer a single-file change and the reviewer must read the gate as well."
